skill.name: drugbank-database
skill.description: Analyze DrugBank data for drug properties, interactions, targets, pathways, chemical structures, and pharmacology research. Use it for licensed DrugBank workflows that require reproducible Python examples and helper functions.
skill.summary: Analyze licensed DrugBank data for pharmacology, interactions, targets, and chemical research.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Static findings were largely false positives from Markdown formatting, DrugBank XML namespace strings, local cache paths, and documented API examples. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found. The main issues are documentation patterns that could expose credentials or encourage unsafe pickle cache loading.

remediation.issue: Command-line examples pass DrugBank credentials as flags.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variables, interactive prompts, or protected config files with restrictive permissions. Avoid examples that place secrets in shell history.

remediation.issue: The cache example uses pickle.load on a local file.
remediation.suggestion: Use a safer cache format such as JSON, CSV, Parquet, or SQLite. If pickle is required, warn users to load only self-created trusted files.

remediation.issue: The config-file credential example lacks file permission guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Document owner-only permissions for local credential files and recommend secret managers for shared or production environments.

semantic_findings.title: Command-Line Credential Exposure Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The data-access guide shows passing DrugBank username and password values through command-line flags. Command-line secrets can be captured in shell history or visible to local process inspection tools.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited CLI example directly includes username and password flags. This is a documentation pattern, not active malware, so medium severity is appropriate.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Pickle Cache Deserialization Example
semantic_findings.description: The caching example loads local pickle data when the cache file exists. If that file is replaced by an attacker or copied from an untrusted source, pickle deserialization can execute arbitrary Python code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly uses pickle loading from a file path. The risk depends on local file trust, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: DrugBank research often needs careful XML parsing, versioned data access, and structured pharmacology queries. This skill provides focused guidance and helper patterns for DrugBank analysis in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Guides DrugBank account setup, versioned downloads, XML parsing, and local cache usage.
Provides helper methods for drug profiles, interactions, targets, and chemical properties.
Explains XML namespace navigation for DrugBank IDs, names, properties, and external identifiers.
Supports drug-drug interaction checks, interaction matrices, and polypharmacy risk summaries.
Covers target, enzyme, transporter, pathway, and repurposing analysis workflows.
Documents chemical similarity, fingerprint, substructure, and ADMET analysis patterns.
limitations: Users must provide their own DrugBank account, license, credentials, and allowed data access.
The skill does not include DrugBank database files or replace DrugBank license terms.
Clinical findings require review by qualified medical or pharmacy professionals.
Some workflows require optional packages such as RDKit, pandas, NetworkX, or scikit-learn.

use_cases.title: Build a Drug Profile Dataset
use_cases.description: Extract names, identifiers, indications, pharmacology fields, and chemical properties from licensed DrugBank XML.

use_cases.title: Review Polypharmacy Interactions
use_cases.description: Check patient medication lists against DrugBank interaction records and summarize possible interaction mechanisms.

use_cases.title: Compare Repurposing Candidates
use_cases.description: Find drugs with shared targets, similar structures, related pathways, and relevant safety considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Find Drug Details
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for one DrugBank identifier.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DrugBank skill to summarize DB00001. Include name, type, indication, mechanism, and main chemical identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Check Drug Interactions
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic interaction review for a small medication list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the interaction workflow to check these DrugBank IDs for pairwise interactions: DB00001, DB00002, and DB00005. Summarize mechanisms and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Target Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Use DrugBank target guidance to profile DB01050. List targets, actions, enzymes, transporters, pathway links, and useful external identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Repurposing Candidates
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced research workflow across multiple evidence types.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DrugBank workflows to compare five candidate drugs for repurposing. Combine target overlap, chemical similarity, indications, interactions, and ADMET concerns.

output_examples.input: Summarize one DrugBank ID for a research note.
output_examples.output: A concise drug profile with identifiers, indication, mechanism, pharmacology fields, chemical identifiers, and cited DrugBank version guidance.

output_examples.input: Check a three-drug regimen for interaction concerns.
output: Pairwise interaction summary for each drug pair.
Plain-language mechanism notes where DrugBank provides descriptions.
A recommendation to verify results with clinical pharmacy review.

output_examples.input: Find structurally similar drugs for a lead compound.
output_examples.output: A ranked research summary with similarity rationale, shared targets, pathway overlap, and follow-up validation steps.

best_practices: Use environment variables or protected secret stores for DrugBank credentials.
Record the exact DrugBank version used in every analysis.
Validate chemical structures and clinical conclusions with domain experts.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real usernames, passwords, or API keys in notebooks or scripts.
Do not treat DrugBank interaction records as direct medical advice.
Do not mix DrugBank versions without documenting the source version for each result.

faq.question: Does this skill include DrugBank data?
faq.answer: No. Users must access DrugBank through their own account and license.

faq.question: Can it download the latest DrugBank release?
faq.answer: It explains use of drugbank-downloader for versioned or latest downloads when credentials and licenses allow access.

faq.question: Can it analyze drug-drug interactions?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides examples for extracting interactions, checking pairs, and summarizing regimen-level concerns.

faq.question: Can it perform chemical similarity searches?
faq.answer: Yes. The references describe SMILES extraction, fingerprints, Tanimoto similarity, and substructure search workflows.

faq.question: Is it suitable for clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. It can support research and review, but clinical decisions require qualified professional judgment.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
